elements.element: Customer has no minimum purchase or volume commitment.
elements.evidence: The redline strikes the floor from Section 4.2.3(ii): the Elected Total Amount now reads "which shall be no more than $120 million," removing the "no less than $110 million and" obligation. PB's election is therefore a ceiling only, with no minimum draw or take-or-pay floor left in the operative text. The overrun-allocation and use-of-proceeds covenants noted in the rationale are cost-allocation/application-of-funds terms, not purchase minimums.

elements.element: Customer pays only for usage or ordered Services.
elements.evidence: Retained Section 6.2 scales consideration to funding actually drawn: "the Approval Payments will be multiplied by a fraction, the numerator of which is such actual amount of Development Costs paid or incurred by SFJ hereunder ... and the denominator of which is One Hundred Twenty Million U.S. Dollars ($120,000,000.00)." Combined with PB's unilateral election of the amount it wants funded, PB pays only in proportion to the funding it orders and SFJ actually provides. (The fragment's opening conditional is truncated in the excerpt; the fixed $120M denominator against actual costs is nevertheless a pro rata mechanic, so no further edit is required here.)

elements.element: The commitment is limited to the current 12-month term.
elements.evidence: No temporal limit was inserted; the election under Section 4.2.3(ii) is a one-time election tied to the Successful Phase 3 Interim Analysis and the multi-year Development Term. The redline targets the preferred level (no floor at all) rather than a 12-month-scoped floor, so this fallback mechanic is simply absent.

elements.element: Customer may reduce the commitment on 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The rendered language contains no reduction-on-notice right; PB's only notice obligation is to "notify SFJ in writing of the total amount of Development Costs ... that PB elects to have SFJ fund." A 30-day downward-adjustment right would have to be drafted expressly.

elements.element: Any shortfall is handled through a true-up rather than a penalty.
elements.evidence: The only true-up in the retained text runs the wrong way: "determine any true-up payments required to be made by PB ... and PB shall pay any such true-up payment to SFJ." There is no shortfall true-up operating in PB's favour, and PB's at-will exit remains subject to the 300% payment under Section 14.2.2 (handled under the liquidated damages rule).

reasons: Preferred level is complete: deleting "no less than $110 million and" eliminates the minimum draw, and retained Section 6.2's pro rata Approval Payment fraction ties PB's payment to Development Costs actually funded, so PB pays only for what it orders/uses.

Minimality holds: the single deletion is confined to the floor language; the $120 million cap, the PB Costs formula, the quarterly payment schedule and all of Section 6.2 (including the $120M denominator and the SFJ-favouring true-up) are left untouched. No survival tails, procedures or extra requirements were added.

Intent is preserved: the $120M denominator in Section 6.2 remains coherent because the cap is unchanged; the PB Costs formula still operates (paying only the excess of the Elected Total Amount over the enumerated deductions) and no cross-reference or defined term is left dangling. Reviewers should nonetheless confirm no other section (e.g., security, termination or minimum-return provisions) keys off the $110 million figure; if one does, a conforming edit is required to avoid a dangling reference.

Fallback is not met and need not be: no 12-month scoping, no 30-day reduction right, and no PB-favouring shortfall true-up appear in operative language. Because the preferred checklist is fully met, the position is complete at the preferred level; the comment's offer of a 12-month/30-day floor is an acceptable concession path but is correctly left out of the operative redline.
